extracted.intended_audience: school and institutional administrators, Title IX Coordinators, lawyers/counsel for LEAs and IHEs, and other recipients of Department of Education funds
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements from the Department of Education's final Title IX regulations and the Regulatory Impact Analysis describing recipients' obligations (grievance procedures, supportive measures, training, notice requirements), expected behaviors, and estimated burdens/costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer and coordination of supportive measures upon notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon being notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX, including sex-based harassment and prohibited retaliation, a Title IX Coordinator must offer and coordinate supportive measures, as appropriate, to the complainant or respondent (final §106.44(f)(1)(ii) and (g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement covers supportive measures offered in response to information that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination (not limited to actual knowledge of sexual harassment). For allegations other than sex-based harassment or retaliation, providing supportive measures does not require the recipient, its employee, or any other authorized person to alter the alleged discriminatory conduct for the purpose of providing a supportive measure. The Department expects the number of times parties will seek supportive measures to increase and includes related costs in its model; types of supportive measures vary by situation and the Department used costs of more commonly provided measures for estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and effective steps to prevent recurrence (hostile environment standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations require a recipient to take prompt and effective steps to ensure that sex discrimination, including sex-based harassment that creates a hostile environment based on sex, does not continue or recur in the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This required use of a hostile environment standard encompasses conduct addressed in enforcement practice prior to the 2020 amendments. The Department anticipates that applying this standard will increase recipient responsiveness to reports and complaints and may deter or prevent some incidents; however, precise reductions in incidents cannot be firmly quantified. This obligation informs recipients' grievance procedures and remedial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures must be prompt, equitable, and adapted to context (§106.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must adopt grievance procedures that are prompt, equitable, and specifically adapted to their unique circumstances, including setting, size, and administrative structure (final §106.45 and related discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have flexibility to design procedures consistent with Title IX that fit their educational environment; the Department expects some recipients to revise procedures and recordkeeping and estimates associated one-time costs. The final regulations remove some 2020-imposed restrictions, allowing procedures that are less burdensome per investigation if appropriately adapted. Recipients in different implementation groups (A/B/C) may experience differing changes in investigation volume and burden per investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide equal opportunity to access relevant evidence and summary investigative reports (§106.46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under final §106.46, recipients may provide parties with an equal opportunity to access the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence or a written investigative report that accurately summarizes the evidence, subject to the requirement to provide access to the underlying evidence upon the request of any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an optional flexibility recipients may use; it affects how investigations are conducted and may reduce burdens compared to more rigid procedures. The Department assumes recipients will exercise such options depending on their context, which factors into cost/burden estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training: timing, scope, and frequency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees must be trained promptly upon hiring or upon change of position that alters their duties under Title IX, and annually thereafter, on the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination (including the definition of “sex-based harassment”) and applicable notification requirements (final §§106.40(b)(2) and 106.44).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department assumes most recipients already provide required trainings annually and will adjust content rather than extend length for most employees. Title IX Coordinators will require more extensive training (the Department estimates 2 hours longer in Year 1 and 1 hour longer in subsequent years) and updated training materials; recipients may use outside counsel, law firms, professional organizations, or internal staff. The Department estimates development and update costs and treats benefits of training (improved compliance and fairness) as justifying the costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting and updating notice of nondiscrimination (§106.8(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must post nondiscrimination statements on their websites consistent with the notice of nondiscrimination requirements under final §106.8(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department assumes a subset of recipients will experience more than de minimis burden to modify existing statements (estimated percentages provided for LEAs, IHEs, and other recipients). For recipients that have not completed the requirement, the Department estimates specific staff hours (e.g., 1 hour Title IX Coordinator + 2 hours web developer) and a one-time aggregate cost. Recipients should review and update online notices to ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must read and understand the final regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: All recipients are assumed to need time to read and understand the final regulations and preamble to determine compliance obligations and necessary policy changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department estimates variation in approach (some will conduct close, time-consuming reviews; others will rely on shorter third-party summaries). For cost modeling, the Department assumed 4 hours each for a Title IX Coordinator and a lawyer per recipient (with aggregate Year 1 cost estimates). This review step is the foundation for subsequent policy and training updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise grievance procedures and recordkeeping to conform to final regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must revise their grievance procedures to conform to the final regulations (including revisions associated with moving from §106.45 of the 2020 amendments to final §106.45 and for IHEs to comply with final §106.46) and update recordkeeping practices accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department assumes specific staff-hour estimates per revision (e.g., 12 hours Title IX Coordinator, 2 hours administrator, 6 hours lawyer per institution) and provides a total one-time cost estimate. The Department anticipates burden increases associated with necessary revision of procedures and recordkeeping across recipient groups, though magnitude varies by prior practice and group classification (A/B/C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage expansion to specified bases of sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Final regulations explicitly cover sex discrimination based on sex stereotypes, sex characteristics, pregnancy or related conditions, sexual orientation, and gender identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department assumes inclusion of these bases may result in an approximate 10 percent increase in the number of investigations conducted annually for recipients that had not fully addressed incidents on these bases; cost models adjust historic data to account for this expansion. Recipients should anticipate handling complaints and offering supportive measures on these bases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow complaints by persons other than students or employees (§106.45(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.45(a)(2) allows a person other than a student or employee who is participating or attempting to participate in a recipient's education program or activity to make a complaint of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department anticipates this change will result in a minimal increase in overall complaint volume because such complaints are relatively uncommon, but recipients (especially Groups B and C) should have processes to address non-student/non-employee allegations via Title IX grievance procedures, alternative disciplinary processes, or other appropriate processes. Group A recipients may only act if the reporting party initiates a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures for non-harassment sex discrimination are limited in scope
rubrics_metrics.description: For allegations of sex discrimination other than sex-based harassment or prohibited retaliation, the recipient's provision of supportive measures does not require altering the alleged discriminatory conduct; many such incidents (e.g., unequal access to resources/facilities or differential treatment by staff) will have few appropriate supportive measures beyond eliminating the source of discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department expects little impact on anticipated costs associated with offering supportive measures in these contexts; supportive measures will often be academic or administrative in nature (e.g., allowing a student to change sections, counseling), and eliminating the source of discrimination (e.g., fixing unequal facilities) is a remedy but not a 'supportive measure' under the definition. Recipients should tailor supportive measures to the nature of the allegation and recognize limits on what supportive measures may entail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and data assumptions for burden estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department relies on median hourly wages, an employer loading factor, NCES and CRDC data, and historical reports (e.g., 2014 Senate Subcommittee Report) to estimate recipient burdens and assumes wide variation across recipient sizes and types when averaging burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RIA describes assumptions (e.g., median wages, loading factor of 2.0, rounding practices for presentation vs calculations) and modeling groups (A/B/C) for estimating number of investigations and costs. Recipients should be aware that estimates are average burdens and actual burdens may be higher or lower depending on institution size, administrative complexity, and prior practices.
